angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 897,453 km at 130.97 pc = 0.09 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 7.6354 +/- 0.0285 mas (same row, RUWE 0.92): 130.97 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.29 +/- 0.04 solar radii from Thomas et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-5108 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...694A.143T/abstract): 897,453 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.1 +/- 0.03 solar masses from Thomas et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-5108 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...694A.143T/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5808 +/- 40 K from Thomas et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-5108 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...694A.143T/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Thomas et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-5108 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...694A.143T/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-5108.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.258, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
